mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to tightened financing conditions for corporate investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in the month prior to the prediction window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening month (two-tailed t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, inflation expectations rise, depressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 5-year rolling window, 60-day forward returns during such inflation spikes are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 10,000 jobs in the prior two months is associated with stronger consumer demand and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-on-month average > +10,000 over the previous two months
failure_condition: During periods of high unemployment, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5% in the prior month coincides with reduced corporate activity and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During periods of high uncertainty, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) show simultaneous monthly increases above their 12-month averages, it signals resilient consumer and business demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-on-month > 12-mo avg AND RSAFS month-on-month > 12-mo avg
failure_condition: In non-recessionary regimes, the 5-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.0% for three consecutive months in a labor market recovery regime is associated with increased hiring expectations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% for 3 consecutive months in a recovery regime
failure_condition: During periods of high inflation, the 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 (GDP chainless) of at least 3% in the quarter prior to the prediction window, in conjunction with FEDFUNDS below 5%, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days due to economic weakness.
failure_condition: During periods of high uncertainty but strong equity performance, the 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE remains above 5.5% for two consecutive months in a deflationary regime, it indicates weak labor demand and a higher probability of supply-side constraints, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.5% for two consecutive months in a deflationary regime
failure_condition: During periods of strong economic growth, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
